thesis: Alphatec is a medical-device company focused on spine surgery through the Alpha InformatiX platform, combining implants, EOS imaging, SafeOp neural monitoring, and the Valence navigation/robotics system. The core surgical business is growing at a double-digit pace with surgeon and procedural adoption expanding more than 20% in Q1 2026, but the stock has sold off 20-32% after a Q1 revenue miss and a 2026 guidance cut driven by underperforming EOS imaging. We rate ATEC SPEC. BUY at $9.55 because the core implant business is healthy, adjusted EBITDA and free-cash-flow guidance were reaffirmed despite lower revenue, and the new $300M refinancing lowers interest expense and extends maturities. The high uncertainty comes from $466M of net debt and convertible-note overhang, competitive pressure from Medtronic, Globus, Stryker, and Zimmer, and the need to execute a turnaround in EOS and the Valence rollout.

drivers: EOS imaging revenue recovers above guided levels and returns to growth
Valence intraoperative navigation/robotics platform gains rapid surgeon adoption and lifts ASPs per case
Surgical revenue growth reaccelerates toward 20% as ATEC continues taking share from Globus, Stryker, and Zimmer
Adjusted EBITDA reaches ~$134M and free cash flow turns positive at ≥$20M, de-risking the balance sheet
Refinancing savings and improved sentiment drive multiple expansion toward analyst consensus targets

base_case.assumptions: Surgical revenue grows at a mid-teens pace, EOS stabilizes near the $77M guided level, adjusted EBITDA reaches ~$134M at ~15% margin, and the refinancing reduces interest expense by more than $6M annually. The stock rerates modestly as free cash flow inflects, but debt/execution risk keeps the valuation below analyst consensus.

risks: EOS imaging continues to weaken and pressures full-year revenue guidance again
Competitive share loss to Medtronic, Globus, Stryker, or Zimmer compresses surgical growth and margins
Valence rollout is slower than expected, limiting the robotics/navigation premium
Adjusted EBITDA or free cash flow miss guidance, raising balance-sheet concerns
Convertible notes and equity compensation create dilution that weighs on the stock

catalysts.event: Estimated Q2 2026 earnings report — first read on whether EOS stabilized and whether EBITDA/free-cash-flow guidance remains intact
Valence intraoperative navigation/robotics platform adoption metrics and any expansion of surgeon/robotics accounts
EOS imaging recovery or restructuring/fix updates
Refinancing savings flowing through interest expense and cash flow
Path to positive free cash flow of at least $20M

key_risks: EOS imaging segment underperforming and dragging consolidated revenue
Heavy debt load (~$466M net debt) and convertible note overhang
Ongoing dilution from equity compensation and convertible securities
Competitive spine market dominated by Medtronic, Globus Medical, Stryker, and Zimmer Biomet
Price pressure in spine implants and hospital cost scrutiny
Execution risk on the Valence navigation/robotics rollout
High dependence on sustained above-market surgical volume growth
